mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE falls below 3.5%, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction starts above 1.75 million units signals strong household demand and rising inflationary pressures, which triggers a hawkish monetary policy response and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1750.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 104.0 index level signals weakening manufacturing activity and a contraction in real output, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 104.0, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both consumer price inflation (CPI) and residential investment (RSAFS) signals a broad-based demand surge that increases inflation expectations and forces the Fed to maintain high interest rates, suppressing equity valuations and leading to negative forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising CPIAUCSL and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a non-significant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate combined with a decline in industrial production signals a policy-induced economic slowdown, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5pp in 1 month AND INDPRO decreases > 0.5pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling INDPRO fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in non-farm payrolls signals a labor market that is both tight and expanding, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to a hawkish Fed response and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a non-significant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) combined with rising residential construction (HOUST) signals strong aggregate demand, which increases inflationary pressures and leads to a hawkish monetary policy stance, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising GDPC1 and HOUST fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
